about: The roots of fish genus names, as a memory aid (Pierre, 2026-11-14, Q124 d: 'Je suis tes recommandations pour tout'), read from The ETYFish Project (etyfish.org), C. Scharpf: genera, by genus name: page, the slug of its ETYFish page (https://etyfish.org/<page>/); ety, the start of its entry there, verbatim; p, the parts that spell the name: [form] an ending or a part ETYFish does not gloss, [form, meaning, word] a meaning and its word, both verbatim in ety (word '' when the entry gives none), [form, genus, '', 'genus'] another genus the entry names, [form, person, '', 'honours'] the person the entry says it honours; fit, optional, one of the genus's own IMR cues the entry says the name refers to. skip: every other circle-1 genus and why it has no line (an etymology unknown or given as a guess, two meanings, a root that points to another IMR cue or reads against one: rules C1, C2). tools/build_fish.py add_families puts root {p, fit, src} on fish.json genera; learn.js rootLine shows it on the sheet the genus opens. Never an invented etymology.

Neopomacentrus.ety: neo-, new, i.e., a new genus of Pomacentrus

Amblypomacentrus.ety: amblys, blunt, referring to short head of A. breviceps; Pomacentrus

Coradion.ety: kore, pupil of the eye; adion, placed sideways (on the flank)

Centropyge.ety: kentron, thorn or spine; pyge, rump or rear

Pygoplites.ety: pyge, rump or rear; [h]oplites, armed (with a weapon)

Pomacanthus.ety: poma, lid or cover; acanthus, thorn or spine

Genicanthus.ety: genys, cheek; acanthus, thorn or spine

Acanthurus.ety: acanthus, thorn or spine; oura, tail, referring to sharp scalpel-like scales on caudal peduncle (hence the common names surgeonfish and doctorfish)
Acanthurus.fit: One scalpel on the tail base

Hipposcarus.ety: hippos, horse, referring to its “typical horse-like snout”; Scarus

Oxycheilinus.ety: oxy, sharp, i.e., a sharp Cheilinus

Labrichthys.ety: Labrus, similar to and/or closely related to both Labrus and Labroides; ichthys, fish

Hemigymnus.ety: hemi-, partial; gymnos, bare or naked

Stethojulis.ety: stethos, breast or chest, referring to thoracic scales as large as, or larger, than those on sides; Julis

Pseudocheilinus.ety: pseudo-, false, i.e., although this genus may resemble Cheilinus

Diproctacanthus.ety: di-, two; procto-, anus; acanthus, thorn or spine

Iniistius.ety: inion, back of head; istius, sail

Hologymnosus.ety: holos, whole or entire; gymnosus, bare or naked

Pteragogus.ety: ptera-, fin; agogos, leading, guiding or attracting

Pseudodax.ety: pseudo-, false, i.e., although this genus may resemble Odax

Wetmorella.ety: –ella, diminutive connoting endearment: in honor of ornithologist Alexander Wetmore (1886-1978)

Lutjanus.ety: tautonymous with L. lutjanus, from Ikan (=fish) Lutjang, local Indonesian name for snappers (although Bloch believed it was from Japan)

Scolopsis.ety: scolo-, thorn; opsis, face or appearance

Epinephelus.ety: epinéphelos, ancient Greek for “clouded over,” referring to film or membrane eye of most if not all groupers known to Bloch (although modern accounts mention only a transparent cornea protruding slightly through the orbit)

Diploprion.ety: diplo-, double or two-fold; prion, saw

Pseudanthias.ety: pseudo-, false, i.e., a false Anthias

Ostracion.ety: ancient name for boxfishes, Latinized from the Greek ὀστράκιον, diminutive of óstrakon (ὄστρακον), shell or shellfish

Parupeneus.ety: para-, near, i.e., close to Upeneus but differing in dentition

Mulloidichthys.ety: replacement name for Mulloides Bleeker 1849, preoccupied by Mulloides Richardson 1843 (=Arripis, Arripidae, Scombriformes), originally –oides, having the form of: Mullus, original genus of type species, M. flavolineatus, but differing in dentition; ichthys, fish

Upeneus.ety: misspelling or incorrectly latinized form of hypene, Greek noun for moustache (or by extension beard)

Balistapus.ety: a-, without; pous, foot, i.e., a Balistes without pelvic fins (actually

Rhinecanthus.ety: rhine, rasp; acanthus, thorn or spine

Pseudobalistes.ety: pseudo-, false, originally proposed as a subgenus of Balistes (i.e.

Oxymonacanthus.ety: oxy, sharp, referring to produced snout of O. longirostris, previously placed in Monacanthus

Pseudomonacanthus.ety: pseudo-, false, i.e., not representing the true form of Monacanthus (original genus of type species M. macrurus)

Pervagor.ety: Latin for to wander over or range through
p: to wander over or range through

Pseudalutarius.ety: pseudo-, false, i.e., not representing the true form of Alutarius (=Aluterus

Paramonacanthus.ety: para-, near, similar to Monacanthus (original genus of P. curtorhynchos) but different in shape of head

Myripristis.ety: myrios (μυρίος), countless or ten-thousand and pristis, saw

Neoniphon.ety: néos (νέος), new, described as “nearly allied” in general form to Niphon (Perciformes: Niphonidae)

Ostorhinchus.ety: osteo-, from ostéon (ὀστέον), bone; rhynchus, from rhýnchos (ῥύγχος), snout

Cheilodipterus.ety: cheī́los (χεῖλος), lip, referring to extensible upper lip of C. lineatus; di-, from dýo (δύο), two, and pterus, from pterón (πτερόν) or ptéryx (πτέρυξ), fin

Pristiapogon.ety: pristis, from prístēs (πρίστης), sawyer (but here likely meaning saw), referring to serrated preopercular ridge of P. fraenatus; proposed as a subgenus of Apogon

Foa.ety: from fō, Samoan name for cardinalfishes

Taeniamia.ety: taenia, from tainía (ταινία), band or ribbon

Saurida.ety: diminutive of Saurus (now a junior synonym of Synodus)

Trachinocephalus.ety: Trachino-, referring to resemblance to weever-fishes, Trachinus (Trachinidae); cephalus, from kephalḗ (κεφαλή), head
